title: Admin procedural packs: modular runbook tasks and automated support hooks
creator: Priya Nair
description: Introduce 'procedural packs' — compact, versioned bundles of idempotent admin tasks (typed inputs, outputs, and metadata) that can be executed from the Console, CLI, or triggered by support automation. Goal: convert frequently used runbook steps into composable tasks with provenance, dry-run, RBAC gates, and telemetry so first-line support can run safe, repeatable remediations without engineering intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Create a procedural pack schema (yaml/json) with typed inputs, optional dry-run flag, and metadata fields for provenance
Implement runtime shim in admin service to execute a pack with safe defaults, idempotency checks, and telemetry emission
Expose packs in Console with run UI, input validation, and 'preview (dry-run)' mode
Add audit logging and RBAC gating so packs require specific role to execute in production
Provide a minimal CLI subcommand to run packs with tracing IDs and link back to Console execution view
Ship 3 initial packs: restart-ephemeral-worker, clear-cache-prefix, and gather-instance-diagnostics, each with tests and playbook docs
comments: 2026-03-01 - Priya Nair: Proposal drafted after support triage workshop; identified 18 high-frequency manual steps that could be automated.
2026-03-03 - Ethan Chen: Spike completed — created prototype YAML schema and a PoC executor that runs in staging with idempotency token checks.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Ava Thompson): Console mockups added for pack run flow; recommended adding explicit confirmation for high-impact packs and a risk label.
2026-03-07 - Security (Diego Martinez): Requested KMS signing for pack manifests and additional audit fields; flagged requirement for formal security review for packs that modify production state.
2026-03-10 - Ethan Chen: Started executor integration tests and added telemetry hooks; created draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-procedural-packs/pull/12
notes: Proto decisions: packs are atomic units that must declare required permissions and a safe 'rollback' hint where possible.
We will avoid embedding credential material in manifests; runtime will request ephemeral tokens from control plane.
Telemetry: each execution emits a trace id, pack_version, caller_identity, and pre/post snapshots of affected resources (where feasible).
Fallback policy: if a pack fails pre-flight checks, it must produce structured diagnostic output and not mutate state.
Rollout plan: enable packs as opt-in in staging for 2 weeks, run audits and chaos tests, then canary to a small set of production orgs
